description: Envelope Factory: a polyphonic envelope generator of 1 to 20 stages, each stage set to move, hold, sustain, rise or fall, with a gate output per stage and a shared trigger output

params.text: Attenuates and inverts the AMP input to set the voltage the envelope calls 100%, that input being normalled to 10V; with VCA mode on it sets the VCA level instead
Attenuates and inverts the OFF input to set a voltage added to the finished envelope, and it starts at 0% so nothing is added; with VCA mode on it sets the velocity response curve instead
Cycles the range of every stage time knob: 0.001 to 10 seconds, 0.01 to 100 seconds, 0.1 to 1000 seconds, or 1 to 10000 seconds
Turned on, a retriggered envelope starts from 0V rather than from the voltage reached
Makes the GATE button a toggle, one press taking the gate high and the next taking it low, in place of a gate that lasts while the button is held
Cycles how the RETRIG input is read: the leading edge of a gate crossing 2V, the instant the voltage starts changing, or the instant it stops changing
Adds 10V to the GATE input while it is high, starting an envelope by hand
Mutes the GATE input for one sample, which starts a new envelope while that gate is held high
Turned on, a 1ms trigger is fired at the STAGE TRIGS output each time an envelope runs to completion; an aborted envelope fires nothing
Cycles what that stage does: Move to the next target over a time, Hold a level for a time, Sustain a level while the gate is high, Rise to 100%, or Fall to 0%
Cycles how that stage ends: Full runs it to completion and refuses retriggers, RTrg lets a retrigger cut it short, and Gate moves on to the next ungated stage when the gate falls
Sets the length of that stage under a Move, Rise or Fall action, on the range the Slow button picks; under a Hold or Sustain action it sets the level instead, 0% for 0V and 100% for 10V
Attenuates and inverts the CV input for that stage's time or level, each volt doubling or halving a time

Bends that stage under a Move, Rise or Fall action, concave up counter-clockwise and concave down clockwise; under a Hold action it is the length of the hold, and under a Sustain action the drift rate
Attenuates and inverts the CV input for that stage's shape, hold time or drift rate
Turned on, the start of that stage fires a 1ms trigger at the STAGE TRIGS output

inputs.text: Speeds up and slows down every timed stage together, each positive volt halving the times and each negative volt doubling them, which gives a looping envelope a volt per octave over its rate
Sets the voltage the envelope reaches at full height, through the AMP knob, and is normalled to 10V; with VCA mode on this is the audio the envelope attenuates
Sets the voltage added to the finished envelope, through the OFF knob, and is normalled to 10V; with VCA mode on this is the velocity, 0V to 10V, sampled as the envelope starts
A rising edge starts an envelope, and the gate holds any sustain stage; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.2V
Starts a new envelope while the GATE input is held high, by muting that gate for one sample; the Retrig Mode button sets what counts as an event here
Shortens or lengthens that stage, each volt halving or doubling its time, or moves its level under a Hold or Sustain action, in each case through the attenuverter above this jack
Bends that stage's curve, or moves its hold time or its drift rate depending on the action, through the attenuverter above this jack

outputs.text: Carries a 1ms trigger at the start of every stage whose trigger switch is on, and at the end of a completed envelope when the EOC switch is on; triggers closer together than 1ms merge into one
Carries 10V while no envelope is running and 0V while one is; the lamp above it glows yellow in proportion to the channels that are idle
The finished envelope: the envelope percentage times the amplitude voltage, plus the offset, so it rests at the offset voltage
The envelope turned upside down, resting at the amplitude plus the offset and falling to the offset; with VCA mode on this carries the audio after the envelope and the VCA
Carries 10V while that stage is running and 0V otherwise; the lamp beside it glows yellow in proportion to the channels in that stage

notes: a newly placed Envelope Factory has four stages set up as an ADSR, which becomes an ADBDR once the sustain stage's drift knob is turned up
patch IDLE into GATE and the envelope loops without stopping; patch IDLE into RETRIG and it loops for as long as GATE is held high
every running envelope is cut off and the module returns to idle whenever a stage's action is changed, the stage count is changed, or the module is bypassed
with the synced VCA mode chosen, each trigger is held back until the audio at the VCA input crosses 0V, which keeps a very fast attack from clicking
there is no oversampling here, so a looping envelope run at audio rates will alias
menu: Stage count — sets how many stages the envelope has, 1 to 20; the module grows or shrinks to match, pushing neighbours right, and cables on a removed stage are deleted
VCA mode: Off, Standard VCA, VCA with 0 crossing synced triggers — turns the AMP and OFF controls and the INV output into a VCA level, an audio input, a velocity input and a VCA output
Randomize configuration — picks which stage controls the Randomize action changes: Stage times, Stage levels, Stage shapes, Stage drifts, Stage attenuverters and Stage triggers

inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 10V.
